title: Infosys ADR Jumps 3.7% as GuruFocus Still Sees Deep Undervaluation
excerpt: Infosys closed at $13.22 in New York even as GuruFocus puts fair value at $18.97, with Q2 results on October 23 set to test the valuation case.
body:
• Infosys ADR (NYSE: INFY) closed at $13.22 on October 22, up 3.69% from $12.75 the previous day, extending a sharp October rebound.
  • GuruFocus rates Infosys 86/100 on its GF Score and puts GF Value at $18.97, implying the stock traded about 30% below that estimate even after the rally.
  • The move comes a day before Infosys reports Q2 FY27 results on October 23, with brokerages expecting 1.1-1.7% sequential constant-currency revenue growth.
  • For US holders, the question is guidance: analysts are split on whether Infosys trims its FY27 growth outlook of 1.5-3.0% or holds it.

Shares of Infosys Ltd rose 3.69% in New York on Thursday to $13.22, from a previous close of $12.75, according to market data reported by Global Banking & Finance. The gain capped a strong run in October for the Bengaluru-based IT services company, whose American depositary receipts had been under pressure for much of the year.

The immediate catalyst in coverage was valuation. A GuruFocus analysis highlighted on Thursday argued the stock remains significantly undervalued after the rally. GuruFocus puts Infosys at a GF Score of 86/100 and a GF Value of $18.97, compared with a price of $11.70 in its valuation snapshot — a discount of 38.3%. Even using Thursday's higher close of $13.22, the gap to that $18.97 estimate is still more than $5 a share.

What the valuation case rests on

GuruFocus bases the score on financial strength, profitability and growth rather than a single multiple. Its page for Infosys notes scaled net operating assets of 0.45 as of June 2026 and lists two warning signs for investors to review. The broader argument in the GuruFocus pieces circulating this week — including one asking whether it is too late to buy after a 3.8% rally — is that the earnings power and balance sheet have held up better than the share price.

That view is not unanimous. Other valuation models using lower growth assumptions produce fair values closer to the current price, and technical trackers note the stock has run quickly in recent weeks. The divergence matters: Infosys is being priced less as a high-growth software name and more as a cash-generative services business whose growth is currently in low single digits.

Results on Friday will test the story

Infosys reports second-quarter fiscal 2027 results on October 23. According to The Hindu BusinessLine, brokerages expect revenue of Rs49,090 crore to Rs49,323 crore, up 1.7-2.3% sequentially, with constant-currency growth of 1.1-1.7% quarter on quarter and profit after tax of Rs8,026 crore to Rs8,100 crore.

Deal momentum is the other check. HDFC Securities expects large-deal total contract value of $2-3 billion in the quarter, down from $3.6 billion in Q1. PL Capital expects EBIT margin to improve by about 40 basis points sequentially as Project Maximus benefits and currency help offset amortisation and AI investment. Emkay noted that part of recent US dollar growth came from the Optimum acquisition, with currency a small headwind.

Guidance is the swing factor

Infosys entered the quarter guiding to FY27 revenue growth of 1.5-3.0% in constant currency and an operating margin of 20-22%. BusinessLine reported HDFC Securities expects a trim to 2-3%, while Emkay expects 1.5-2.5%. A cut would not by itself break the undervaluation case if margins and cash flow hold, but it would confirm that discretionary spending by clients in financial services, retail and manufacturing remains soft.

For investors who bought the ADR for income and stability rather than rapid growth, the more important numbers on Friday may be margin, free cash flow conversion and large-deal wins. Infosys has in prior quarters shown strong cash conversion even when growth slowed, a pattern that supports the GuruFocus financial-strength rating.

What to watch next

Watch the October 23 results release and call for three things: whether guidance changes, whether large-deal TCV recovers toward the Q1 level, and whether management comments on AI-led deals offsetting pressure on traditional work. If guidance is held and margins stay inside 20-22%, Thursday's valuation argument will look stronger. If guidance is cut and deal wins fall, the discount to GF Value may persist for a reason.

This is not investment advice. Valuation models differ widely on Infosys depending on growth and margin assumptions, and readers should check the full results filing before acting.
